The findings sum to -0.4 and the scaled number is +0.4 (p_up 52 x abs 10). Both are inside the noise. They differ in sign only because p_up also carries the washed-out setup (-28% from the Sep 24 high, below the $95 August offering price), which I filed small as a finding.

findings.finding: Intel has beaten its own revenue guide by wide margins two quarters running while demand exceeds supply and it raises prices. Q1 2026 was $13.58B vs $12.39B estimates. Q2 2026 was $16.13B vs a $13.8-14.8B guide and $14.42B consensus. Price actions continue: Intel confirmed July consumer and server CPU price revisions, and DigiTimes reports a further ~10% PC CPU increase around Oct 5. So Q3 revenue at or above the $16.8B top of guide is likely, against a $16.45B consensus only ~1% above the guide midpoint.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: a 12% revenue beat and a raised guide went +12-13% after hours and closed about -5 to -8% on Jul 24, sold on capex. Q1 2026: a ~10% revenue beat closed +23.6% on Apr 24. Beats have been both bought and sold.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. If the market expected another 10%-scale beat, consensus would sit near or above $16.8B, not $16.45B. The buy-side whisper is unobservable and is probably higher than consensus. The stock is 25% off its high into the print, which is not what a crowded beat expectation looks like.
findings.independence: Pricing evidence from a separate source: DigiTimes via xenospectrum, 2026-09-08 (https://xenospectrum.com/en/intel-october-cpu-price-hike/), reports the ~10% October PC CPU hike as unconfirmed and notes that Intel confirmed the July revisions. Q1 beat figures are from https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/mizuho-revamps-intel-stock-price-122743528.html (snippet).

findings.finding: The PC market fell harder in Q3 than a 'sub-seasonal' assumption implies. IDC (Oct 8) has Q3 2026 shipments at 62.7M, -20.1% y/y and -9.1% q/q, against a normal seasonal rise. IDC says the channel was clearing inventory built in H1 ahead of memory-driven price hikes and that 'the outlook for the coming quarters will worsen before it gets better'. Gartner (Oct 12) has -22.4% y/y. In July, management guided H2 PC consumption 'sub-seasonal' and full-year 2026 down low double digits. CCPG ($8.9B in Q2, ~55% of revenue) faces a sell-in headwind into the Q4 guide. Net of the rest: Intel is supply-constrained and says weaker client frees wafers for higher-value DCAI ($6.3B, +59%). That makes this a mix shift more than lost revenue, so it is sized small.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Jan 2026: a Q1 guide below consensus took the stock about -17%. Client weakness was flagged in July without a visible price penalty at the time.
findings.why_not_priced: The data has been public for three weeks and the stock fell about 10% since, so it is largely priced. What is not priced is how Intel's Q4 CCPG guide translates a -20% unit market that is worse q/q than seasonal. If fully priced, the Q4 consensus ($16.92B, +4% q/q) would have been cut toward flat. I could not see a cut.
findings.independence: Gartner, 2026-10-12, -22.4% y/y to 55.4M (https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2026-10-12-gartner-says-worldwide-pc-shipments-declined-22-point-4-percent-in-third-quarter-of-2026-as-component-cost-inflation-raised-asps). The management guide of 'sub-seasonal / low-double-digit decline' is from the Q2 call (https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/intel-q2-earnings-call-highlights). Proxy: this is industry units, not Intel's own number.

findings.finding: Q4 guide upside from supply and price. On the Q2 call, management said supply growth is 'skewed toward the end of the third quarter and into the fourth quarter, especially for servers'. Server CPU lead times run up to six months and prices are up 10-20% since March. A ~10% PC CPU price increase is reported for early October. Together these lean toward a Q4 revenue guide above the $16.92B consensus. That consensus is single-source, so this is capped small.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: the Q3 guide came in well above consensus ($16.3B midpoint vs ~$15.0-15.1B), yet the stock closed down on capex. Q1 2026: a raised Q2 guide was bought +23.6%. Q4 2025: a Q1 guide below consensus drew about -17%. The guide is the line this stock trades on.
findings.why_not_priced: Q4 consensus of $16.92B is only ~4% above the Q3 guide midpoint. That is roughly normal seasonality, with nothing added for the supply step-up or the October price action. If priced, Q4 consensus would sit near $17.3-17.5B.
findings.independence: Server CPU pricing and lead times: TrendForce/Reuters/CRN via search (https://www.trendforce.com/news/2026/03/13/news-intel-reportedly-says-cpu-supply-tightness-is-affecting-all-customers-chromebooks-hit-hard/). The October PC price hike is DigiTimes via xenospectrum (unconfirmed), which shares a document with finding 1's pricing evidence. Offsetting: the PC destock in the finding above.

findings.finding: On the Q2 call Intel said 2027 capex will be 'significantly above' the 2026 level of more than $20B. The CFO said he rejected his teams' first number. Consensus models negative FCF in 2026 and 2027. A first 2027 capex figure on this call is the likely negative, because the July print was sold on exactly this line despite a large beat. The $19.7B net equity raise in August and the 25% drawdown since reduce the shock value.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Jul 24, 2026: the capex raise from $18B to over $20B, with 2027 'significantly above', was cited as the reason a 12% revenue beat closed about -5 to -8% (Sahm Capital and Traders Union headlines that day).
findings.why_not_priced: Direction is known, size is not. If priced, sell-side 2027 FCF would already reflect a specific number. TIKR says consensus has FCF turning positive only in 2028 and that a big 2027 step-up 'without new revenue visibility would pressure the multiple'. A number well above ~$25-30B would still surprise.
findings.independence: TIKR (https://www.tikr.com/blog/intel-stock-fell-5-in-a-day-as-chip-stocks-sold-off-ahead-of-its-october-29-report-heres-where-the-stock-could-go) quotes Zinsner's 'no' to his teams and the FCF path. The Q2 release is the primary source for capex >$20B.

findings.finding: Gross margin faces cost inflation. In July the CFO flagged memory and substrate cost inflation as a live H2 risk. The Q3 non-GAAP GM guide is 42.0%, only +0.2pt over Q2's 41.8%, and Q2 beat its own GM guide by ~280bp on pricing. The Q4 GM guide versus 42% is called the swing factor by Mitrade. Only the cost side is filed here; the pricing side sits in findings 1 and 3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: a 280bp GM beat did not stop a down day. No clean history of a GM miss in 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: GuruFocus and Heygotrade frame 42% as 'the hurdle', so the bar is known. Memory contract prices rose 13-18% in Q3 (TrendForce via SK hynix coverage) after the guide was set, so cost may exceed the July assumption.
findings.independence: SK hynix Q2 commentary and TrendForce Q3 DRAM contract +13-18%: https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/sk-hynix-operating-profit-rises-557-percent (proxy). Mitrade 2026-10-25 on the Q4 GM swing.

findings.finding: The GAAP escrow derivative probably swings to a gain in Q3. About 143M Department of Commerce escrowed shares are carried as a derivative liability marked to INTC's price. The stock went from $128.32 on Jun 26 (Q2 end) to $123.00 on Sep 25 (likely Q3 end), implying roughly a $0.76B GAAP gain in interest and other. Q2 had a $12.5B loss on the same line. GAAP EPS could therefore print well above the $0.31 guide. This is non-operating and excluded from non-GAAP.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: the $12.5B escrow loss produced an -$11B GAAP net loss, and the market looked through it.
findings.why_not_priced: Nobody trades INTC on GAAP EPS. The only effect is headline optics ('GAAP profit' instead of the Q2 'loss'). The share count may have changed with transfers.
findings.independence: Q2 charge confirmed by the Q2 8-K. Jun 26 close $128.32 from https://kalkine.com/news/technology/intel-corporation-nasdaqintc-falls-342-as-intcs-comeback-trade-faces-a-fresh-test. Sep 25 close $123.00 from https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/intc/history/.

findings.finding: The $20B equity offering (210.5M shares at $95, closed Aug 12, plus a 31.6M greenshoe) came after the July EPS guide. It adds roughly 2-2.5% to the time-weighted Q3 diluted count, about -$0.01 on a $0.38 guide, partly offset by interest income on $19.7B. Answer to what the money buys: capacity for a supply-constrained order book (10 long-term data-centre supply agreements, server lead times up to six months). So the financing funds visible demand and nets to about zero.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None on a print. The offering priced at $95 on Aug 10; the stock is now ~$92-95.
findings.why_not_priced: Sell-side models most likely updated the share count. This is filed for completeness, at zero.

findings.finding: On Oct 14 an explosion with nitrogen trifluoride at Intel's Kiryat Gat site killed two to three workers. Fab 28 there produces Intel 7, which supplies supply-constrained Raptor Lake and Xeon parts. Intel has made no public statement on production. Any Q4 supply impact would first be quantified on this call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No precedent. The stock fell 2.8% on Oct 15 along with peers.
findings.why_not_priced: Not quantified anywhere. One Chinese-language summary attributes 'minimal impact' to Intel, which is unconfirmed. If priced, analysts would have cut Q4 Intel 7 supply, and no such note was found.
findings.independence: Mitrade 2026-10-25 notes 'Intel has not commented on any production impact'. https://www.gadgetreview.com/?p=420244 covers the same event.

findings.finding: Foundry optionality. The 14A PDK 0.9 was slated for external customers in October 2026. A preliminary Apple-Intel foundry agreement has been reported (WSJ via Tom's Hardware) but not confirmed. Policy cuts against disclosure: the CFO said Aug 26 that Lip-Bu Tan 'does not want to be announcing customers on the foundry side'. A named commitment on the call is a low-probability upside. Q2 external foundry revenue was $293M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Foundry headlines have moved the stock sharply. Jan 28, 2026 surged on Nvidia/Apple foundry reports; Oct 5, 2026 was -4% on Musk's Terafab/TSMC talks.
findings.source_date: 2026-10 (PDK timing; exact date not confirmed from URL)
findings.why_not_priced: Policy says no announcement, so the market assigns little probability. If priced, the stock would not have fallen 4% on the Terafab/TSMC headline.
findings.independence: Tom's Hardware on the WSJ preliminary Apple deal (https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/semiconductors/apple-reportedly-strikes-deal-for-intel-to-make-some-of-its-chips-two-tech-giants-reached-a-preliminary-agreement-for-intel-to-make-processors-for-cupertino). The non-disclosure policy is from TIKR.

findings.finding: The setup is washed out. INTC fell from $127.39 (Sep 24) to $95.53 (Oct 28), -25%, and -23% over 20 sessions. That is below the $95 August offering price, with RSI ~30. Most of the decline is sector or macro (SOX -6.72% on Oct 22, the OpenAI revenue report Oct 8) rather than Intel-specific. Intel's outlook was unchanged and no 8-K was filed after Aug 12. Short interest is low (~2.4% of float), so there is no squeeze mechanism. This lowers the bar for the reaction, not the number.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In July the stock ran into the print near highs and the beat was sold. In April it came in after a selloff and was bought +23.6%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a statement about what is priced, not an unpriced fact. Sized small because 20-day run-up reversal is a free control and not research.
findings.independence: Mitrade 2026-10-25 (https://www.mitrade.com/insights/news/live-news/article-8-2192144-20261025): 'Intel's own outlook was unchanged', with the SOX drop and the Susquehanna PT cut to $105.

findings.finding: A reported delay of Diamond Rapids (next P-core Xeon) to mid-2027, leaked late July 2026, has not been confirmed by Intel. The call could confirm a roadmap slip against AMD Venice.
findings.why_not_priced: The leak is three months old and the market has largely absorbed it. Confirmation would add little.
findings.independence: 3dnews 2026-07-31 (https://3dnews.ru/1142700/). Igor's Lab carries the same leak.

findings.finding: Customers who reported after Intel last spoke keep raising compute spend. Meta (Oct 21-22) raised its 2026 capex floor to $135-145B, posted Q3 capex of $34.9B, and disclosed ~$825B of AI data-centre and compute commitments, up from ~$700B in July. Microsoft said in July that Azure is capacity-constrained through at least end-2026. This supports DCAI demand (agentic CPU demand was the Sep 21 rally thesis). Intel's binding constraint is supply, not demand, so this does little for the quarter itself.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Sep 21, 2026: +12.1% on Meta Muse/agentic CPU demand headlines.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The market read Meta's spend as an AI-funding worry, and INTC fell 8% that day. A demand read that the market took negatively is unlikely to add much.
findings.independence: Microsoft July call on capacity constraints (https://www.thestar.com.my/business/business-news/2026/07/31/microsoft-sees-strong-cash-flow-lower-capex). Trefis 2026-09-29 on the Sep 21 Meta Muse CPU-demand move.

outside_window.finding: The Apple 14A foundry deal (~$10B reported, 2029 production), if ever confirmed, and 14A risk production in 2H 2027 resolve far beyond the window unless announced on the call; the in-window optionality is filed in findings.
Mercury Research Q3 2026 x86 share data (Q2 was Intel 69.3%, first time below 70% since 1995) usually publishes in November, after the window.
AMD reports in early November. A share read-through from its server and client numbers lands after INTC's exit window.

lessons_applied: Rule 1 (verified fact is not a reaction): Q3 beat finding cut +1.5 to +0.8, because the July 12% beat closed down 5-8%.

Rule 6 (bar): Q4 consensus is single-source (Benzinga snippet), so the Q4-guide-upside finding is capped at +0.8 from +1.5. The capex finding moved -1.5 to -1.2 since its size also leans on the Q4 call framing.
Rule 9 (net of the rest): PC-TAM finding cut -1.5 to -1.0, since Intel is supply-constrained and shifts wafers to the +59% DCAI segment.
Rule 5 (positioning / unexplained drawdown): washed-out setup cut +1.0 to +0.5. It is a free-control restatement, not research.
Rule 4 (financing is a question): the dilution item went from -0.1 to 0.0 because the money funds capacity for a supply-constrained order book.
